ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the table in the figure lists the percentages of rare earth reserves, production, and consumption of some countries and regions in the world in 2009. China's rare earth reserves account for 36%, production accounts for 97%, and consumption accounts for 41%; the United States' reserves account for 13%, production 0%, and consumption 13%; Japan's reserve data are missing, production 0%, and consumption 26%; other regions' reserves account for 51%, production 3%, and consumption 20%. Then reason: China bears 97% of production with 36% of reserves, indicating that rare earth production and resource consumption pressure is too great. From the perspective of sustainable development, exports of primary mineral products should be reduced, and protective mining of rare earth resources should be carried out; vigorous mining or expanding the export share should not be done. This question only asks what type of mineral products should have their exports reduced, so it corresponds to “primary mineral products.”
